metadata.creator: Branch Education
metadata.description:
How do Microchips work?  How does your smartphone camera work?  How does Bluetooth work?  At Branch Education, we dive deep into the science, engineering, and technology in our modern world using 3D animation and incredibly detailed models. 

Founder of Branch Education: Theodore J Tablante

Want to support in-depth engineering and technology education? Support us on Patreon:  http://www.patreon.com/brancheducation

Modeling is done in Blender 4.2.3 LTS Eevee and Cycles Render Engine, Adobe Premiere, and Reaper

https://branch.education/

Go watch the real thing as long as it is still exist, this is just an archive for history and for the coming generations!

metadata.title: The Death of Educational Content on YouTube
metadata.creator: fern
metadata.description:
The Death of Educational Content on YouTube

by dwinni

Published at YouTube on September 6th, 2026
_________________________________________________________________________

A compilation of videos done by various YouTube and other content creators across all time or spaces. There isn't a structured nor defined objective with archiving this apart from the sake of it. Perphaps they might contain useful to you, perphaps not yet, nonetheless, they contain with it the memory and wisdom of people that once stood and breathed just like you.
_________________________________________________________________________

An examination onto how the operations and business models of AI-generated channels manage to mass produce low-quality video that automate plagiarism and spread misinformation while threatening manual productions

Video's Description:

FlexiSpot Labour Day Sale is here - up to 65% off sitewide! Use code FERN50 to get an extra $50 off on all products.
Check out the E7 Pro Standing Desk:

Countless AI slop channels are relentlessly copying our work. So one day we decided: enough is enough. We went undercover to investigate who’s behind them and what this flood of AI slop means for the future of educational content on YouTube.

Many thanks to Dr. Akhil Bhardwaj, Prof. Dr. Andrea Löw, neo, Memeable Data and The Present Past for their valuable insights.

_____

Armchair documentaries, almost weekly

@Grv328's Comment:

I hope someone invents an “AI block”, like Ad block, so I can just never see AI slop channels

@fbianconi's Comment:

This wouldn't be such a problem if YouTube decided to just bring back thumbs up/down ratios

@YotaNinja's Comment:

The craziest part to me, about all of this, is Youtube had a somewhat effective method of dealing with this already in place, that they removed years back. The Like to Dislike ratio bar was a great indicator of whether or not a video was legitimate and informational.

@howa08's Comment:

The way to combat this is to not watch them. Good work Fern & all the other original creators.

@ewr_plane_spotter's Comment:

Your anger comes through in this video and it's warranted

@besmart's Comment:

What's really fun is when you get to hear your own voice on some of these AI channels, because it was illegally cloned and sold by AI dubbing companies. Because that's what happened to me! If anyone hears my voice narrating slop, rest assured it's not actually me
I guess I could take it as a compliment, that people just want to be me. But it's really just sad and pitiful.

@SeriousHistory's Comment:

Holy shit. That Lumicus channel at 10:14 literally just took my character and put a hat on it. I looked at their channel and of course its AI slop attempting to make animated videos. This is so ridiculous.

@TorredeControlNews's Comment:

As a creator who a lot of hours manually recreating flight paths and cockpit procedures in flight simulators for air crash documentaries, this hits way too close to home. The worst part isn't just the theft, it's the viewer skepticism. People now look at a meticulously crafted 3D Sim scene and instantly wonder if it's low effort AI slop. And YouTube shouldn't allow this, because they're the first to analyze videos using AI, and then they allow and give views to AI  slop content while failing to reward real content created with effort. Thanks for bringing light to this, Fern. Real human research and editing need to be protected more than ever.

@febstone's Comment:

I must sadly admit. when I first saw fern (with the Japan metro video), I thought it was an AI slop channel, due to the relatively smaller size of the channel at the time, and the 3D thumbnail. This is the real danger, mistaking real videos with slop, which may lead to an easier disbelieve of real content and fact, locking you into a known or given way of thinking

@JacksonPhixesPhones's Comment:

Don't forget that YouTube's slop ID system is demonetizing legit channels that are not AI slop. Legit channels get scraped by AI, the scraped data is used by slop channels to copy/plagiarize legitimate channels, and so the legitimate channels get struck in a full-circle slop avalanche moment. Super gross.

——————————————

Archived with the purposes of preservation.
